line: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. Last film, you steered a task live. This one runs itself — while you sleep, while you're in another meeting, while you're on the train. Scheduled tasks. While you were away.
screen: Hook card reading 'while you were away?' A clock face beside a task card; small task rows check off on their own.

line: Three terms. A scheduled task: a Cowork task that runs on a clock, not on your say-so. Cadence: how often — hourly, daily, weekdays, or manual. A run: one execution — its own fresh session, every time. Keep those three.
screen: Three term cards appear one by one: 'scheduled task — runs on a clock, not your say-so' / 'cadence — hourly, daily, weekdays, manual' / 'run — one execution, its own fresh session'.

line: Film two was steering — you were there, giving direction mid-task. But Cowork can also work on its own, running tasks on a schedule while you focus on something else. No steering. No watching. The task has a clock, and the clock does the managing.
screen: Split card: left side greyed 'steer it live' (film two); right side in terracotta 'runs on a clock' with a clock face. Caption: 'the clock does the managing'.

line: Here's the demo's example. Tell Claude: every hour, check the content team's shared drive folder for documents added or modified. For each one, note who made the changes and summarize what's new. Group the changes by client. Save the summary as a doc in my daily updates folder. One sentence of intent — the whole job.
screen: Instruction card labeled 'one sentence of intent': five mini-rows check off — 'check the drive' / 'note who changed what' / "summarize what's new" / 'group by client' / 'save to daily updates'.

line: You don't hand-write the schedule. Claude drafts a prompt for the scheduled task, and you review it. Want hourly instead of daily? Weekdays instead of every day? Change it — cadence is a dial, not a contract. When everything looks right, you accept the proposal. Only then does the task exist.
screen: Draft card labeled 'draft — you review': cadence chips 'hourly' 'daily' 'weekdays' 'manual' appear; a green 'accept' check lands. Caption: 'cadence is a dial, not a contract'.

line: Accept, and Claude creates the scheduled task and pins it to the scheduled page in the left sidebar. That page is mission control: every task, its cadence, its next run. Nothing hides in a menu. If it's not on that page, it's not scheduled.
screen: Sidebar mock: left sidebar with 'Scheduled' highlighted; one task row with its cadence and next run. Label: 'mission control'.

line: Claude runs it automatically while your desktop app is open. And here's the part that matters: each run executes as its own Cowork session, with fresh context. Not yesterday's context — today's. So Claude always works from the latest state of your files and your connected tools.
screen: Two session cards labeled 'run one' and 'run two', each stamped 'fresh context'. File icons behind them refresh. Caption: 'the latest state of your files'.

line: One honest constraint. For a scheduled task to run on its cadence, your computer needs to be awake, and the Claude desktop app needs to stay open. Laptop shut for the flight? A run gets missed. But nothing is lost — Cowork runs it as soon as you're back, and tells you it was delayed.
screen: Laptop card: 'awake + app open' with a green check. Below, a timeline: a missed run in grey, then 'you're back' — the run fires in terracotta with a 'delayed' tag. Caption: 'nothing is lost'.

line: The scheduled page is also where you stay in charge. Review past runs. Edit the instructions. Change the cadence. Or trigger it on demand — right now, don't wait for the clock. Scheduling is not surrendering control. It's choosing when you exercise it.
screen: Control panel card: four rows — 'review past runs' / 'edit instructions' / 'change cadence' / 'run now'. Caption: 'you stay in charge'.

line: And everything you connected still works on the clock. Any connectors you've set up are available for scheduled tasks — calendar, drive, Slack, all of it. A scheduled task sees what you see. The clock doesn't shrink the toolbox.
screen: Toolbox card: connector chips 'calendar' 'drive' 'Slack' beside a clock. Caption: "the clock doesn't shrink the toolbox".

line: Picture the morning. You open your laptop. In your daily updates folder: a digest, grouped by client, every change noted, every author named. You didn't check the drive. You didn't ask anyone. The work happened while you were away. That's the whole film in one folder.
screen: Morning card: a folder labeled 'daily updates' opens; a digest doc with three client rows, each checked. Caption: 'the whole film in one folder'.

line: So what belongs on a schedule? The film's rule of thumb: schedule the recurring, skip the one-off. If you do it every week and the steps don't change — digest the drive, sweep the inbox, prep the standup — that's a schedule. If it needs your judgment mid-flight, steer it live, like film two. Clock work versus steering work.
screen: Two columns: 'clock work — recurring, same steps' with a green check vs 'steering work — needs your judgment' with a steering marker. Caption: 'clock work versus steering work'.

line: And this series walks the map in order. Next film: Tag Claude In — we put Claude inside your team channel and draw the exact line around what it can and cannot see. Then the verification loop, a year of Claude Code, all the way to the AI-native company. Ten films. Three done. The walking continues.
screen: Series map card: ten dots in a row, the third highlighted; caption 'Next: Tag Claude In'.

line: Let's recap. A scheduled task runs on a clock: you approve the draft, pick the cadence, and it runs while the app is open. Each run is a fresh session on the latest state of your files. Missed runs catch up when you're back. Review, edit, or trigger on demand from the scheduled page.
screen: Recap card. Four lines appear one by one: 'a scheduled task runs on a clock' / 'each run is a fresh session on today's files' / "missed runs catch up when you're back" / 'review, edit, or run on demand'.

line: Your turn. Pick one recurring chore — the drive digest, the inbox sweep, something weekly. Write the one-sentence instruction you'd give it, and the cadence. Then check: is it clock work or steering work? If it's clock work, you just wrote your first scheduled task.
screen: Your-turn card: 'Pick one recurring chore. Write the one-sentence instruction.' Below it: 'Clock work or steering work?'
